title: A Cipher for the Portrait
premise: Jude Dunmore, the concierge of the Marlowe Grand Hotel, has built a career on noticing without being noticed — until a nervous stranger pays a month in advance for one service: prove that a murder scheduled to happen hasn't happened yet. The predicted victim is Edith Vane, whose family fortune rests on a portrait that conceals the truth of a death thirty years ago, and every alibi in town was woven by people who were there. As Jude pulls threads through ledgers, letters, and the hotel's own guest registers, they discover the 'client' is not trying to prevent a murder but to force the town to finally confess an old one. In the end, Jude exposes the original killer — the beloved hotel owner who raised them — and must choose between the belonging they always craved and the identity of someone who refuses to keep secrets anymore.
about_author: Astrid Sterling spent a decade working night desks at grand old hotels before turning her habit of eavesdropping into fiction. She writes mysteries about the people who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A gray-eyed guest calling himself Mr. Ash books a month at the Marlowe Grand, pays cash, and asks for one thing: proof that Edith Vane will still be alive on the first of next month. Jude's instinct says scam; their instinct also says fear. Emotional beat: unease — the invisible observer suddenly has skin in the game.

chapters.title: The Portrait's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Researching the Vane family for Ash's file, Jude learns Edith's brother Thomas vanished thirty years ago the same week the famous portrait was unveiled. Old staff whisper that the painter never painted from life. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the past starts pressing against the present.

chapters.title: Alibis, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using seven years of discreetly kept records, Jude maps where every surviving witness claims to have been the night Thomas disappeared — and finds three alibis that match too perfectly, word for word. Emotional beat: the thrill of pattern-recognition shadowed by the realization someone taught the town its story.

chapters.title: What the Concierge Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Ash POVs. Ash reveals he is Thomas's son, raised abroad on his father's letters, which stop abruptly mid-sentence. He believes Edith knows how they end. Meanwhile someone ransacks Jude's office. Emotional beat: alliance forming between two people who don't trust anyone.

chapters.title: The Guest Register
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the hotel's archived registers, Jude finds the killer's mistake: a name crossed out but legible under raking light — registered under a false name the very night Thomas vanished. The handwriting belongs to someone still on the payroll. Emotional beat: vertigo; the safe harbor may be the storm.

chapters.title: Edith Breaks Her Silence
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Under pressure from both Jude and anonymous threats, Edith admits she saw something thirty years ago and traded silence for her inheritance. She gives Jude half the truth and a warning: the person you're looking for made you. Emotional beat: grief and complicity — inheritance bought with a buried body.

chapters.title: A Room Not on the Books
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the register lead, Jude finds a sealed service corridor behind the portrait's original hanging wall, and evidence Thomas never left the building. Ash goes missing after promising to meet Jude there. Emotional beat: isolation — the helper has become the hunted.

chapters.title: The Confession Scheduled
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, captive. Ash confronts his captor alone and learns the murder 'predicted' was bait: the killer needed Jude to dig until the proof surfaced, then planned to erase both of them. Ash stalls by offering the missing final letter. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Everything Noticed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Luring the killer — hotel owner Marguerite Hale, who took Jude in as a teenager — into the corridor with a staged ledger reveal, Jude uses thirty years of the woman's own habits against her while police, tipped by Edith, close in. Marguerite confesses to Thomas's accidental death and its thirty-year cover-up. Emotional beat: heartbreak and clarity colliding.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, resolution. The portrait is cleaned, revealing Thomas's face beneath the varnish, and the town finally buries him. Ash leaves Jude the letters and a standing invitation; Edith endows the hotel's archive in Thomas's name. Jude, no longer filing secrets but keeping records, signs their own name to the finding. Emotional beat: quiet belonging earned honestly, at last.
